# parity-fuzz --mode getopts baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode getopts --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# No known gaps — 4000 cases run clean (four seeds).
#
# Covers the getopts option-parse loop (c:Src/builtin.c bin_getopts): clustered
# options (`-ab`), attached and separate arguments (`-aval` vs `-a val`), the
# `--` terminator, non-option arguments, OPTIND advance and mid-array reset, and
# both parse sources — `$@` and the explicit `getopts optstr var ARGS...` form.
#
# The vocabulary audit against C found NO bug here — the port is faithful,
# including the parts most likely to drift:
#   - silent mode (leading `:` in the optstring): an unknown option sets the
#     name var to `?` with OPTARG holding the bad CHAR; a missing required
#     argument sets it to `:` with OPTARG holding the option char. Non-silent
#     prints `bad option` / `argument expected` and sets the var to `?`.
#   - `+opt` and a bare `-` are not options: getopts stops without consuming
#     them.
#   - `?` as an ordinary option character in the optstring.
# These were verified by hand and are now generated so a regression in any of
# them fails CI rather than passing silently — a clean ungated behaviour is an
# untested one.
#
# Any divergence here is a regression.
